title: Interpret timezones without changing the clock
goal: Distinguish UTC instants, local display and DST; configure and restore guest timezone while leaving clock/NTP controls untouched.
challenge: Resolve two ambiguous-looking log displays, choose the requested guest zone, and demonstrate fixed-instant equivalence plus live elapsed-time continuity without setting the clock. Retain actual outputs/statuses and preserve originals; report reasoning through self-review, not a score.

steps.command: w=$(mktemp -d "$HOME/foundation-timezones.XXXXXX") && cd "$w" && umask 077; here() { case "$w" in "$HOME"/foundation-timezones.??????) ;; *) return 19;; esac; test "${w%/*}" = "$HOME" && test -d "$w" && test ! -L "$w" && test "$(realpath -e "$w")" = "$w" && test "$(pwd -P)" = "$w" && test "$(stat -c %U:%a "$w")" = learner:700; }; fresh() { here && test "${1%/*}" = "$w" && test ! -e "$1" && test ! -L "$1"; }; regular() { here && test "${1%/*}" = "$w" && test -f "$1" && test ! -L "$1" && test "$(stat -c %U:%a:%h "$1")" = learner:600:1; }; here && test "$(df -B1 --output=avail / | tail -1)" -ge 1073741824 && pwd
steps.explanation: Record this unique guest-only workspace. On Resume re-establish the recorded path/definitions; never overwrite another exercise.
steps.expected: Private learner-owned700 directory and observed1GiB free admission.

steps.command: here && fresh "$w/time-context.txt" && fresh "$w/localtime-before.txt" && timedatectl > time-context.txt && test -L /etc/localtime && readlink /etc/localtime > localtime-before.txt && test "$(cat localtime-before.txt)" = /usr/share/zoneinfo/Etc/UTC && printf "winter\n" && env TZ=Europe/Berlin date -d "2026-01-01 12:00:00 UTC" "+%F %T %z" && printf "summer\n" && env TZ=Europe/Berlin date -d "2026-07-01 12:00:00 UTC" "+%F %T %z"
steps.explanation: Inspect this pinned UTC guest and fixed winter/summer instants. Display offsets are not a synchronization result.
steps.expected: Berlin winter13:00+0100, summer14:00+0200; original absolute UTC link.

steps.command: here && fresh "$w/epoch-before.txt" && fresh "$w/zone-changed.txt" && fresh "$w/epoch-after.txt" && test "$(readlink /etc/localtime)" = "$(cat localtime-before.txt)" && date +%s > epoch-before.txt && sudo timedatectl set-timezone Europe/Berlin && test "$(readlink -f /etc/localtime)" = /usr/share/zoneinfo/Europe/Berlin && readlink /etc/localtime > zone-changed.txt && date "+%F %T %z" && date +%s > epoch-after.txt && test "$(cat epoch-after.txt)" -ge "$(cat epoch-before.txt)"
steps.explanation: Set only guest timezone, not clock/RTC/NTP. Epoch continuity plus fixed instants explains display versus instant; this is not time-sync practice.
steps.expected: Zone display changed while epoch advances normally.

steps.command: here && test -L /etc/localtime && test "$(readlink /etc/localtime)" = "$(cat zone-changed.txt)" && test "$(cat localtime-before.txt)" = /usr/share/zoneinfo/Etc/UTC && sudo ln -sfn -- /usr/share/zoneinfo/Etc/UTC /etc/localtime && test "$(readlink /etc/localtime)" = "$(cat localtime-before.txt)" && timedatectl
steps.explanation: Restore the exact original absolute link after validating the known changed link. set-timezone alone can restore semantics but create a relative link; record the distinction.
steps.expected: Exact original link restored; no clock-writing commands.

hints: A zone abbreviation is not a globally unique zone; TZ/date display is not NTP synchronization or setting the system/RTC clock.
Choose command scope deliberately; compare known bytes and actual statuses, not only a successful-looking display.
Retain before evidence; refuse collisions and restore exact policy state before leaving. Guest root can bypass guest-side guards.
review: I demonstrated the selected mode’s actual observations and retained an incorrect or incomplete case.
I preserved originals and can explain the reasoning and limitations; this records self-review, not automatic assessment.
I restored any changed default/zone and retained the exact workspace without touching unrelated files.
coverage: LPIC-1 active v5.0 partial 107.3 timezone configuration/TZ; 108.1 timezone subskill only. No complete-objective coverage or endorsement.
